default.py:25 limits _NO_ILIKE_DIALECTS to {mysql, sqlite} (postgres excluded), and line 93-95 emits the guidance only for those. Neither MySQL nor SQLite has an ILIKE operator (a statement using it is a syntax error). LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER('pat') is a standard, working case-insensitive match on both. Tried input: non-ASCII pattern (e.g. 'É' vs 'é') on SQLite, where built-in LOWER folds only ASCII. It does not match, but plain LIKE and any other built-in alternative behave the same, so the advice is still the correct general substitute. A MySQL binary/_bin column is likewise a collation-specific edge case and does not make the guidance wrong.

factory.py:83-90,186 use the same cfg.database.url for build_sql_runner and sqlglot_dialect_for_url, whose result feeds DefaultSystemPromptBuilder(dialect=...). sqlglot_dialect_for_url (safety/readonly.py:99-110) returns the _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT key that the scheme starts with (postgres, mysql, sqlite). build_sql_runner (factory.py:224-262) picks SqliteRunner, PostgresRunner and MySQLRunner on startswith sqlite, postgres and mysql, and raises ValueError for any other scheme before the prompt is built. So the engine named in the prompt (_ENGINE_NAMES, default.py:18) is the engine run_sql executes against. Hostile input traced: a SQLAlchemy-style scheme such as postgresql+psycopg2 maps to postgres in both functions, and a scheme matching neither raises. The builder rejects unknown dialects (default.py:52-55), and dialect=None gives the engine-neutral prompt with no engine claim. The claim describes what the agent should do, and the prompt names the correct engine.

default.py:19-23 lists the examples. In readonly.py, _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT (121-125) plus _SHARED_CATALOG_SCHEMAS (119) give postgres {information_schema, pg_catalog} and prefix pg_, mysql {information_schema, mysql, sys, performance_schema}, sqlite prefixes sqlite_ and pragma_. is_introspection_query (176-246) returns True for a Table whose db is in the schemas (240-241) or whose name starts with a prefix (244). So postgres information_schema.columns and pg_catalog.<tbl> both classify as introspection. mysql information_schema.columns does too. sqlite sqlite_master matches the sqlite_ prefix. A SELECT on any of these parses to exp.Select, which is in _ALLOWED_ROOT_TYPES (249-255). It has no DML/DDL, no INTO and no denied function (the denylists at 303-433 do not name these tables), so assert_select_only (607-660) accepts it. Each catalog is also a real introspection target on its engine. Absolute-claim trace: the bare `pg_catalog` text is a schema, so the agent writes e.g. pg_catalog.pg_tables, which classifies True. A bare pg_tables is also True through the pg_ prefix.

registry.py:21-26 TRUNCATED_TOOL_CALL_MESSAGE: "Your call to '{tool}' was not executed: your response reached the output token limit before the call's arguments were complete." Returned at registry.py:198-205 when tool_call.truncated, before validation. Validation failure result is f"Invalid arguments: {e}" (registry.py:212), so it starts with "Invalid arguments"; agent.py:63 defines the same prefix and uses it at :866. The prompt (default.py:113) is a conditional ('If a tool result says...') that paraphrases the truncation message accurately. Those results are not claimed by the prompt's conditional rule and retrying shorter would not help, so no requirement is broken.
